en.name: Peter
en.summary: The apostle whom Catholic tradition holds as the first Bishop of Rome, martyred there under Nero and regarded as the foundation of the papacy itself.
en.body: A Galilean fisherman originally named Simon, Peter was given his new name by Jesus, who called him the rock on which the Church would be built. After the crucifixion he emerged as the leading figure among the apostles, and Catholic tradition holds that he traveled to Rome and served as its first bishop, giving the city's church a preeminence it has held ever since. He is traditionally said to have been crucified upside down during Nero's persecution of Christians, at his own request, considering himself unworthy to die in the same manner as Jesus. The Basilica of St. Peter is built over the site long venerated as his tomb.
